newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs close sharply lower, Telebras plunges.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs close sharply lower, Telebras plunges.

text.p: Brazilian stocks ended 3.35 percent lower, with benchmark Telebras leading the profit-taking and plunging 4.57 percent to 165.10 reais, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 47 most active shares lost 456 points, closing at 13,153 points.
Market turnover was 1.144 billion reais ($1.06 billion).
Traders said a correction in prices was more than expected as local stocks have surged over 90 percent so far this year.
Only Telebras preferred posted gains of over 100 percent in the first half, and many analysts said a correction would be healthy to allow investors to rebuild positions in the stock.

But traders were surprised at how sharply the bolsa fell today and some attributed it to nervousness in the futures exchange market due to a currency devaluation in Philippines just two weeks after Thailand's devaluation of the bhat.
Even those who attributed the fall partly to speculation over the impact of the devaluation in Philippines said it served as an excuse to push share prices down.
"It was more an excuse. The market needed to take a breather," one trader said.

Analysts also said cash inflows are the factor setting the market's trend. After the bolsa's spectacular rise in the first half, equity analysts now expect the market to keep rising, but moderately by year's end.
They said they noted some equity funds, which have been behind the bolsa's most recent rally, are already reducing their buy orders as many stocks have already become expensive.

Other telecom stocks followed Telebras' behaviour and surged over four percent following the announcement of the winning bid for Sao Paulo cellular phone concession, gave back part of its gains, falling 3.9 percent to close at 370 reais.
Telerj fell 6.67 percent to 161 reais, while Telemig lost 4.03 percent to close at 188 reais.
